ARCS kitMolecule 45fact-tile

Fact Tile

Give one fact a label, a figure and a short caption, with the label outside the box so a row of tiles reads as one aligned band.

States

Anatomy

#PartType roleToken (CSS variable)
1LabelAbove the box, left-aligned with its edge, 4px gap; mono-free sans caps, 0.75rem boldcyan
2BoxDrawn behind the figure and caption rows only (a ::before on the subgrid), so the label sits outside itsurface, border, ds-r-sm
3FigureHeadline size, bold, tabular figures, 12px from the box toptext
4Caption0.9rem, 6px under the figure, 12px from the box bottomtext-secondary
5RowA .ftiles-c container (container queries) holding the grid of tiles; each tile spans three subgrid rows so labels, figures and captions line up across the rowrow gap 14px

Usage

Use it when

  • A handful of headline facts (price, length, start, what you get) read better side by side than in a sentence.
  • Use four or two tiles so the breakpoints never leave an orphan; inside a summary disclosure, three or more fit with auto-fit.

Do not use it when

  • Do not repeat a fact the next block already states; drop the tile instead.
  • Do not use it for a probability or a stat with a source line; that is 29 Tile (kept unchanged for its four consumers).
  • Do not put the label inside the box or right-align it.

Data it reads

FieldTypeRequiredNote
tiles[][label, figure, caption]yesLabel is one or two words; figure is short ($4,800, 5 days); caption is one plain line.

Access

  • A ul with an aria-label (such as Step 1 at a glance); each tile is an li reading label, figure, caption in order.
  • All sizes are rem and the row uses minmax(0,1fr), so the largest text size and roomy spacing wrap inside the box instead of overflowing.
  • Contrast: label cyan and caption text-secondary are AA on surface in both themes.
